title: Compare long numeric prerelease identifiers without int conversion (python-semver issue #487)
import_hint: from semver import Version   (package lives in src/semver; the class is semver.version.Version)
statement: python-semver (src/semver, BSD-3) is a semantic-versioning library whose central class is semver.version.Version (also exported as semver.Version). Bug report (upstream issue #487): Version.is_valid("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000) is True, but Version.parse("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000).compare(...) raises ValueError, because Version._nat_cmp in src/semver/version.py converts every all-digit prerelease identifier with int() and CPython refuses int conversion of strings longer than 4300 digits. Fix the prerelease comparison in src/semver/version.py so that it never converts a long ASCII numeric identifier to an int, while keeping the existing ordering rules exactly. Required semantics of the prerelease comparison: identifiers are the dot-separated parts of the prerelease string (an empty or None prerelease has one empty identifier); an identifier consisting only of ASCII digits is numeric and compares by its decimal value, computed without int(): strip leading zeros (an all-zero identifier becomes "0"), compare by length first and then lexicographically; a numeric identifier is lower than any non-numeric identifier; two non-numeric identifiers compare as plain strings; when every identifier of the shorter list is equal, the longer list is higher. Preserve the constructor's legacy behaviour: Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=...) accepts identifiers with leading zeros and identifiers written with non-ASCII decimal digits (str.isdigit() is true), and such non-ASCII digit identifiers keep comparing by their int() value, so "١٢" compares equal to "12" and "１２" is lower than "13"; an identifier for which str.isdigit() is true but int() fails (for example "²") must still make compare() raise ValueError, eagerly, even when an earlier identifier would already decide the order, but only when the core versions are equal: a difference in major, minor or patch is decided before the prerelease is examined, so Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease="²") < Version(1, 0, 0, prerelease="²") is True. Keep everything else unchanged: Version.parse keeps rejecting non-canonical prereleases such as "01", "01.2", "١٢" and "１２" with ValueError; build metadata is ignored in comparisons; a version with a prerelease is lower than the same core version without one; the prerelease attribute is stored as given. Do not change parsing, the optional native parser, tests, docs or packaging files, and keep the whole existing pytest suite passing.
acceptance_criteria: With v = "0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000: Version.is_valid(v) is True; Version.parse(v).compare(v) == 0; compare(v, "0.0.0-2") == 1 and compare("0.0.0-2", v) == -1 (no ValueError).

Ordering of long numeric prereleases with Version.parse("0.0.0-" + x): "9" * 4999 < "1" + "0" * 4999; "1" + "0" * 4998 + "1" < "1" + "0" * 4998 + "2"; "1" * 5000 < "alpha"; "alpha." + "1" * 5000 < "alpha." + "1" * 5000 + ".1". For each pair low.compare(high) == -1, high.compare(low) == 1 and sorted([high, low]) == [low, high].
Build metadata is ignored and release order is preserved: with version = Version.parse("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000), version == version.replace(build="other") and version < Version(0, 0, 0).

Constructor prereleases compare with the legacy rules, as Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=left).compare(Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=right)): ("0001", "1") -> 0; ("000", "0") -> 0; ("02", "10") -> -1; ("01.2", "1.2") -> 0; ("2a", "10a") -> 1; ("01a", "1a") -> -1; ("-1", "0") -> 1; ("", None) -> 0; ("١٢", "12") -> 0; ("１２", "13") -> -1; ("1٢", "12") -> 0; ("٠٠١", "1") -> 0; the reverse comparison gives the negated result and both .prerelease attributes are stored as given.
Version.parse("0.0.0-" + p) raises ValueError for p in ("01", "01.2", "١٢", "１２").
Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=left).compare(Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=right)) raises ValueError for (left, right) in (("²", "2"), ("a.²", "b.0"), ("a.0", "b.²")).
Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease="²") < Version(1, 0, 0, prerelease="²") is True (the core comparison decides before the prerelease is examined).
The existing pytest suite in tests/ passes unchanged.

upstream.reference: upstream issue #487, fixed by pull request #488 (merge commit 1d515915d50b31f23fd1fb0f572ef608453e80e3); the held-out tests are the pull request's own additions to tests/test_compare.py
